feedback.problem: Which of the following gives the equation of the tangent to the curve $r(t)=⟨3t+5,1-{t}^{3}⟩$ at the point where $t=0,$  valid for all  real values of $u?$
feedback.worked_solution:
At the point where $t=0,$ the vector ${r}^{′}(0)$ is tangent to the curve, so the tangent line to the curve at $P$ can be parametrized as
 

$$
R(u)=r(0)+u{r}^{′}(0),\,u\in (-\infty ,\infty )
$$

 

First, we find $r(0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}r(0) & =⟨3(0)+5,1-{0}^{3}⟩ \\  & =⟨5,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

   

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3t+5),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-{t}^{3})⟩ \\  & =⟨3,-3{t}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we evaluate ${r}^{′}(t)$ at $t=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(0) & =⟨3,-3(0)^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨3,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the tangent line to the given curve at the point where $t=0$ is

$$
R(u)=⟨5,1⟩+u⟨3,0⟩,\,u\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
